cells.tense: Right now you're the one deciding which of these hard things you stay with.
cells.act: carry on with the version you chose through another week of doubt
cells.ask: Take the hard thing you've already decided to stay with. Keep the same version of it going one more week — no revised plan, no confirming sign. When the week is out, look back at what you actually did. Nothing changes; you simply continue.
cells.core:
You know what to attend to. Something in you sorts which of the things at hand is worth your attention before you could explain the sort, and the loud one seldom wins. When difficulty settles in, that knowing keeps you from scattering. You put your attention on what still deserves it and you keep it there, and doing that doesn't grind you down the way it grinds others. Attention placed well, day after day, with nobody checking.

A good stretch looks like the same hard thing staying chosen while the days stay full. Feed it hope you've already tested once. No new direction to find, just a return to the one you picked — the same small step, the next day no more certain than the last. The flatness you feel isn't a cue to switch; it's what steady looking costs. Stay with it and the thing gets room to become what it was going to be.
cells.sheetLine: You already chose what to stay with. Stay with it.
cells.verb: to keep going while the conditions stay hard
cells.place: where you decide what deserves the first of your attention

cells.tense: You're already bracing for a stretch that hasn't happened yet.
cells.act: give one thing and take one thing, in balance
cells.ask: Inside this hard season, hand one person something that takes effort, then accept what they offer back without turning it down or evening the score on the spot. Both directions, once, then let it be done. Being received is allowed.
cells.core:
The persistence in you has stopped being a way of lasting and turned into a way of getting out in front of the difficulty. You're up the road already with arms out, holding a weight that isn't there yet, and bracing harder reads as strength from where you sit. From outside it looks like someone nobody gets to take care of, because they'd resist anyone being even with them. What this part of you does well is contain pressure rather than crush it — hold, not out-wait the sky.

Test a small piece of exchange. Choose a person inside the difficulty, give something that takes effort, and accept what they offer without evening it up on the spot. Sit in the awkwardness; that's the part that's been absent. What you take in doesn't cancel what you gave, and letting both stand is what fairness is when it's alive rather than tallied. Try it once.

cells.tense: The hard stretch you were standing in is already over — you're still holding the posture.
cells.act: do the giving in the open this time, where it was always done unseen
cells.ask: Think of something you did for another person and still do. Where they can watch, let the next time happen — the counter, the kitchen, the car. No speech, no asking for credit. Just move that one act out of hiding.
cells.core:
You got through that stretch by picking up what needed picking up, and now the picking-up keeps going past what it was for. You're braced against a past difficulty that's finished. That's the inner picture — the persistence runs on, aimed at a space already dark and empty, so it can't find anything to be for. The strange result is that the strength you built in there looks to you like nothing at all; nobody marked it, so you don't count it.

What restores it is putting a piece of it where a person can see. Not telling the story to a crowd, but letting the next part happen where the one it's for can look — the lunch packed at the table, the last bill settled while they're still up, the drive home made before anyone's asleep. Stand in the spot where the effort happens and let it be seen there. Then it lands somewhere real instead of vanishing into habit.
cells.sheetLine: That hard season is done. The bracing has outlasted it.

cells.tense: The persistence in you is going all on its own, and you don't count it as yours.
cells.act: keep following the star after everything that has happened
cells.ask: Whatever direction you took up before things got hard — keep going that same way through the next uncertain stretch, with no proof it's working. Notice it was yours to choose, and keep going because it was.
cells.core:
There's a persistence running in you that you've stopped hearing. The same difficulty gets met again and again, day after day, and your own account slides past it — conditions, not work. You don't count yourself as someone who holds. That version of you got put away somewhere and left there, and what you keep doing anyway is the person who chose it, declining the easy version whenever it came around.

So make the choice legible again. Return to the simpler form — the direction you picked before anything got hard, picked again when it got hard, and are picking now in the span where nothing is settled yet. Notice it was a choice before anyone told you to hold on. That kind of continuing is yours, and it's been yours since before it got tested.
cells.sheetLine: The grip that keeps going is yours, and no one's told you.

attempts.check: The draft's riskiest claim is that this person's steadiness shows itself as a private, interior enterprise — the record gives the mechanism but not whether anyone else was ever in the room. A reader could say the difficulty is plainly about money or housing, and I'd have narrowed their life into a metaphor; the asks are all acts they can do inside their own week, so they survive that being wrong. The sentence that serves me more than them would be a clean image of 'carrying quietly while no one watches' — true to the mechanism, but a picture I'd be writing for myself rather than from what reached me; it's replaced in every cell.
